title: Choose AfterDegree's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Placement Noticeboard. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Placement Noticeboard
options.lineage: The college placement-cell noticeboard every Indian engineering student checks in season
options.thesis: Outcomes posted like shortlists on the placement board, every number attested in violet ink.
options.viewport: Green rail nav with 8 tools; 'People like you' home as a pinned shortlist with your row highlighted and attested counts.
options.risk: Becomes a cork-board costume if notices are skewed or pinned instead of laid out as a clean product grid.

raised.raise: Fixed-column rankings: rows rerank, columns never move, changed rows stay marked until seen.
Module discipline: every panel carries a small header tab and hairline rules, no whitespace inflation.
One dominant answer per screen: the main result owns the largest panel, everything else supports it.
Fixed furniture: every company or program card shows count, coverage and date in the same spots.

options.label: Metro Line Map
options.lineage: Delhi and Namma Metro line diagrams and station signage
options.thesis: Careers drawn as metro lines: routes, interchanges and the station you are aiming for.
options.viewport: Signage-style top bar and rail; the home shows your cohort's routes as coloured lines converging on destinations.
options.risk: The most familiar choice: transit maps are a common career-path metaphor, so it can read as expected.

options.label: Boarding Pass and Gate Board
options.lineage: Boarding passes and airport departure boards
options.thesis: Your profile is the pass, your options are flights on a board that reranks as evidence changes.
options.viewport: A segmented profile pass (From college, To goal) above a ranked board of programs and routes.
options.case: Students going abroad identify instantly; weaker for universities and professionals not travelling.
options.risk: Leans on the travel cliche if the pass becomes decoration rather than the profile summary.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: The market is terrain; your route rides above it in one reserved purple.
options.viewport: Terrain-tinted panels for markets, with your planned route as a purple numbered course over them.
options.case: Clearest fit for routes and saturation; few Indian users know orienteering maps.
options.risk: Contours and map colours can overwhelm tables if not held to the data layer.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Every result a row on a live departure board.
options.viewport: A full-width board of postings and routes.
options.case: Fuses as a job-posting board only; the whole product does not read as a board.

options.label: High-Density Modules
options.thesis: Pack every answer into ruled modules.
options.case: Too dense for a guided, warm mentor product.
options.kept: Module header tabs and hairline discipline.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.thesis: Each tool a coloured lobe of land.
options.case: Playful tone undercuts evidence and trust.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Companies as a ranked roster of characters.
options.case: Cute register conflicts with serious money and career decisions.
options.kept: Fixed personal furniture on every card.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean career-analytics product, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, greeting, KPI cards and charts for your cohort.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other analytics products by design.
